**Visual observations:**

- **Plant part**: Corn leaf (blade and midrib visible)
- **Leaf blade**: Numerous small, round to oval yellowish-to-tan spots scattered in broad bands across the leaf, with clear alternating bands of infected and non-infected tissue
- **Midrib**: Distinct dark purplish-to-black oval spots running along the central vein — very prominent
- **Pattern**: The banding pattern is characteristic — infected zones alternate with green healthy tissue

**Reasoning:**

This is a textbook match for **Physoderma_brown_spot**:
- Small tan/yellow lesions in broad bands across the leaf blade ✓
- Alternating infected/non-infected tissue bands ✓
- Dark purplish-to-black oval spots on the midrib ✓ (the most diagnostic feature)

No other class fits this combination. Southern rust produces pustules (not banded lesions). Tar spot has raised black stromata that can't be rubbed off. The banding + midrib dark spots together are unique to Physoderma.
